new.headline: Week one was clean, so next week adds only one extra minute of running, on Saturday, with the same three days and easy effort. Your mid-October goal of 30 minutes without walking is too soon, so I would leave the date open.

flags.title: Morning-after shin check
flags.detail: Check the shin each morning after a run. Stop and walk if it aches during a run. Pain above 3/10, or worse the next morning, means we repeat or shorten a session instead of adding.

flags.title: Pain-free weeks
flags.detail: 1 of 4 done. Every run at 0/10 and a quiet shin the next morning counts. Any pain, even if it settles, restarts the count. Until you have four in a row, everything stays easy, with no strides or hills.

flags.title: Mid-October goal
flags.detail: 30 minutes without walking is too soon on a safe build. Keep it as the target, but drop the date until you have a few more clean weeks.

flags.title: Pace on the short running bits
flags.detail: Your running bouts were about 6:45/km at effort 3/10. Hold that or go slower. One-minute bouts tempt you to speed up, and speed is not what this phase is for.

flags.title: Saturday's extra round
flags.detail: This is the only step up. If Monday or Wednesday leave the shin unhappy, run Saturday as 5 rounds like the others.

new.analysis:
Week one went as well as a return week can. You ran all three planned sessions, pain stayed at 0/10, and your shin was quiet afterwards. Heart rate averaged 121 to 123 bpm and peaked at 130, around 68 to 69 percent of your max, so nothing was strained. Nothing needs correcting.

The next step is small because the running volume is small. Going by your splits, each session held about 5 minutes of running, so roughly 15 minutes for the week. Ten percent of that is a minute and a half, which is why I added one round to Saturday and nothing else. The three days stay as your physio set them, and the longest continuous run stays at one minute.

Holding easy effort matters more than it looks. A clean first week counts as one of the four pain-free weeks I want before any strides, hills or faster running. Your shin can feel fine while load quietly builds, so small steps with a morning check are the safest way to build.

Your goal of 30 minutes without walking by mid-October does not fit this progression. The longest continuous run can only grow by 2 to 3 minutes at a time, and you are starting from one-minute bouts. Over the next four weeks your weekly running minutes would climb from about 16 into the low 20s. I would rather set a new date after two or three more clean weeks than promise one now.

At your next visit, tell your physio how the week went and what the plan adds. If anything about your shin changes, they should decide the next step, not the plan.
